summary: Current evidence is sparse for firsthand Java coding questions explicitly tied to 0–2-year QA/SDET interviews. No question was independently verified as having been asked. Use core practice for coverage and never infer frequency from this small source set.

sources.title: Java Programs Asked in SDET Interviews (Tested)
sources.caveats: Author presents a preparation collection, not a dated candidate interview. Claims about repetition or code testing belong to the author and were not independently verified. Adapt solutions to explicit input contracts and Java 8 compatibility.

sources.title: Coding Interviews for SDET and QA Automation Roles
questions: Summarize ERROR log entries by service
Compare expected and actual API response maps
Find the first unique test ID
sources.caveats: These are representative preparation exercises. They are not evidence of a specific company asking them during the research window.

sources.title: Interview Solved #5 EPAM — SDET Interview Decoded

sources.caveats: Publisher attributes questions to an unnamed candidate. Exact interview date and location are absent. This is above the target experience range; use simple collection exercises only as supplemental practice. Sample article code uses records and List.of, which are not Java 8 features.

sources.publicationDateEvidence: Search-index rendering provides Tuesday October 06 2026; opened Reddit page uses relative age. Absolute date is search-index evidence rather than a visible absolute page timestamp.

excludedEvidence: LinkedIn posts with relative ages or crawl dates but no reliable publication date were not used as recent-question evidence.
A TraceLink SDET-1 community report mentions anagrams and duplicate strings, but its stable publication date could not be established; it was not used as within-window evidence.
An EPAM Reddit thread was initially published before the window and concerned seven years of experience; in-window comments do not make the original thread a new report.
bankPolicy: All independently authored exercises without a specific eligible source are Core interview practice. A matching preparation article is Recent preparation resource, never Recently asked. No frequency claim is supported.
